title: Assistant Manager - RCM Business Excellence
description:
NEOLYTIX
   

  

 Assistant Manager, RCM Business Excellence
   

  

 Revenue Cycle Management \| Governance \& Performance \| Gurugram
   

  

 DEPARTMENT
   

  

 RCM Business Excellence
   

  

**Experience**
 6–8 Years
   

  

 LOCATION
   

  

 Gurugram (Onsite)
   

  

 SHIFT
   

  

 India Hours \| US AM Overlap
   

  

 REPORTS INTO
   

  

 President \& COO
   

  

 ⚠ This is not a delivery role. You will not run RCM accounts, manage billing teams, or handle client escalations. You will own the independent measurement layer that tells leadership whether delivery is doing what it committed to do. If you want to go deeper into governance and analytics rather than climb an operations delivery ladder, read on.
   

  

**About The Role**
 Neolytix is a US\-headquartered healthcare managed services organization running RCM, credentialing, and provider services for 270\+ provider organizations across the US. Our delivery teams operate from Gurugram, Manila, and Chicago.
   

  

 We are creating a new seat: Assistant Manager, RCM Business Excellence. This is the founding role of an independent governance function. You will sit alongside delivery, not inside it: your mandate is to define what good process looks like for every RCM account, measure whether it actually happens, and give leadership numbers they can act on. Quality assurance reports to you. You define the metrics, own the cadence, and build the function as it scales.
   

  

 The shift is India business hours with overlap into the US morning for leadership reviews. This is not a night shift role. If you have spent your RCM career on a night shift at a BPO, that changes here.
   

  

 What You Will Own
   

  

* Process SLA Conformance
* Define the committed process standard per RCM account: charge lag, posting turnaround, AR touch cadence, denial resolution timelines, and aging thresholds.
* Track actual performance against committed standards at a granular level. Strategic accounts reviewed weekly, the rest monthly.
* Flag risks proactively with proposed solutions before they breach SLAs.
* Monthly Performance Insight
* Build the monthly performance pack from daily productivity and quality data. The standard: a reader can act on it without asking a follow\-up question.
* Breaches carry a named owner and a resolution date. Last month's breaches are re\-checked before new ones are raised.
* Contribute to weekly and monthly dashboards shared with delivery leadership and, where relevant, clients.
* Quarterly Financial Review
* Analyse financial performance across all RCM accounts: charges, collections, AR aging, denial rate, net collection rate, and cost to collect.
* Present trends to senior leadership each quarter. You will be supported in building this, and expected to stand behind your conclusions when challenged.
* Quality Function Ownership
* Line management of the Quality Lead and QA analysts. You own the sampling plan, audit calendar, scoring consistency, and auditor calibration.
* Ensure QA findings reach the floor and drive change, rather than living in a report.
* Audit team output for accuracy; identify recurring error patterns and drive corrective action.
* Process Change Measurement
* When a new coding guideline, SOP, or process rule goes out, measure whether it was adopted and what it did to denials or rework.
* Rule issued, adoption measured, impact quantified, result fed back. Close the loop, do not just report the issuance.


 What You Bring
   

  

 Must\-Have
   

  

* 6 to 8 years in US healthcare RCM operations, with hands\-on exposure to AR and denials and a working understanding of how process failure shows up in revenue.
* Experience building a reporting, MIS, or business excellence function from scratch: defining the metrics, sourcing the data, establishing the cadence. Inheriting and running a function is not the same thing.
* Fluency in RCM financial metrics: net collection rate, AR aging distribution, denial rate, first\-pass yield, cost to collect. You can explain what moves each one, not just report the number.
* Advanced Excel and working SQL. You use SQL to validate data, not to list it as a skill.
* Confidence presenting findings to senior leadership and holding a position when challenged. This means publishing numbers that make delivery look bad when the numbers say so.


 Strong Preference
   

  

* Six Sigma Green Belt or equivalent process excellence training you have actually applied to a live project, not just certified.
* Experience across multiple billing platforms (AdvancedMD, Athenahealth, Kareo, Epic, Centricity, or similar) and the data normalisation that comes with it.
* Prior management of a small quality or audit team.
* Power BI familiarity, though the analytics team owns the front end.


 Nice\-to\-Have
   

  

* Healthcare analytics firm or BPO process excellence background.
* Experience designing and running an MIS reporting function in a US RCM environment.
* Exposure to SSAE\-18 or SOC 2 audit readiness in an RCM context.


 Who You Are
   

  

* You publish findings that make the delivery team look bad, and you sleep fine afterward. If you soften conclusions to keep the peace, this is the wrong seat.
* You build something and then measure whether it worked. The artifact is not the point; the change it produced is.
* You ask what a number means before you report it. A chart that describes what happened is the beginning of the work, not the end.
* You would rather be right and uncomfortable than comfortable and wrong.


 Eligibility Criteria
   

  

* Education: Graduate degree, any discipline. An analytical or healthcare\-adjacent background is preferred.
* Communication: Excellent spoken and written English. You will present to the COO and CEO quarterly. Communication below this standard will not progress past the screening stage.
* Shift: India business hours with US morning overlap for leadership reviews. Onsite, Gurugram.
* Notice Period: Up to 60 days preferred. Beyond 60 days considered only for an exceptional profile.


 Performance Expectations
   

  

 What success looks like across the first year:
   

  

* Day 30: a current\-state assessment published that honestly names what can and cannot be measured today. No softening.
* Day 60: SLA conformance tracking live for strategic accounts.
* Day 90: SLA conformance extended to the full RCM book.
* Month 3 onward: monthly performance pack running reliably. Leadership reads it and acts on it.
* Year 1: four quarterly financial reviews delivered and defended, MIS Analyst hired and producing independently, at least one process change closed end to end with adoption measured and impact quantified.
* End of year 1: the business argues from your numbers rather than about them.


 Career Path
   

  

 This is the founding seat of a function, not a standalone role. Business excellence and governance are established career tracks in RCM that run to Director and VP level at the large players. We are building ours from its first hire.
   

  

 Now
   

  

 AM, RCM Business Excellence
   

  

 RCM book: quality and MIS
   

  

 12–18 Months
   

  

 Manager
   

  

 Team of 3–5; governance across RCM
   

  

 Next
   

  

 Senior Manager / AD
   

  

 Governance across service lines
   

  

 Beyond
   

  

 Director / VP, Business Excellence
   

  

 The function at company scale
   

  

 The move to Manager is earned against stated milestones, not time served. The rungs beyond it describe where the function is heading as the business grows.
   

  

 Hiring Process
   

  

* Stage 1: TA screening call (30 minutes). Role fit, domain depth check, and shift confirmation.
* Stage 2: Functional interview with the COO (45 to 60 minutes). Process knowledge, multi\-account RCM experience, measurement approach, and how you handle findings that are unwelcome.
* Stage 3: Analytical exercise. A take\-home case using real account data with a genuine deterioration in it. You have 3 days to complete it. We are watching whether you reach for root cause or describe the chart.
* Stage 4: Conversation with the CEO (45 minutes). Scope discussion, career trajectory, and how you think about building a governance function.
* Stage 5: Reference checks (minimum 2 calls). Specifically: an occasion when this person delivered findings that were unwelcome, and what happened next.
* Stage 6: Offer.


 Why Join Neolytix
   

  

 Founding Seat of a Function
   

  

 You own this from its first hire. The metrics, the cadence, the standard: none of it exists yet. That is rare at this level and reads strongly on a CV.
   

  

 Scope from Day One
   

  

 The whole RCM book, not one account or one process. At AM level in most RCM organisations you own a slice. Here you own the view across all of it.
   

  

 Day Shift, Not Night
   

  

 India business hours with US morning overlap. Not a night shift role. If you have spent your career on a night shift, this changes here.
   

  

 AI Makes This More Important
   

  

 As automation absorbs transactional delivery work, the measurement and governance layer becomes a larger share of the organisation. We are building an RCM platform now, and its analyst roles report into this function.
   

  

 Questions? Reach out to Lakshay at Neolytix Talent Management \| This document is confidential and for internal use only

title: Software Development Engineer III
description:
**What is Hunch?**
 Hunch is a dating app built for follow\-through \- designed to turn mutual interest into a real first date instead of another chat thread that fizzles out. Built for people tired of mindless swiping and commodified matchmaking, Hunch uses an AI matchmaker to cut the week of back\-and\-forth and get two interested people out of the app and into the same room.
   

  

 With 2\.4M\+ daters, 1\.47M\+ dates planned, and 100% photo\-verified profiles, Hunch is growing fast in the US by challenging the swipe\-left/right norm of traditional apps. Hunch is a Series A funded ($23 Million) startup building the future of social discovery in a post\-AI world.
   

  

 Link to our fundraising announcement
   

  

**Key Offerings Of Hunch**
* One Drop a Day: A small, hand\-picked set of photo\-verified profiles arrives daily \- chosen for taste, lifestyle, and who's actually free to meet. So every profile gets real attention instead of a mindless swipe.
* Interest Becomes a Plan: When both people want to meet, Hunch's AI matchmaker turns mutual interest into a confirmed date with a real time and place \- no logistics to manage.
* Every Match, Verified: Every profile is matched to a live photo before it appears in anyone's drop. No bots, no catfishing \- just real, trustworthy connections.
* Built to Move: Chats close after seven days and users hold a few conversations at a time \- nudges designed to get people out the door, not scrolling forever.


**About The Role**
 We're on the lookout for a SDE\-III to join our lean, dynamic team as we scale. We believe in pushing boundaries, challenging the status quo, and embracing diversity of thought. You'll be building fast, smart, and with purpose — and we're looking for someone who can lead that charge both technically and culturally.
   

  

**What You'll Do**
* Own backend features end\-to\-end — product problem to API, schema, migration, tests, and deployment. You solve the problem, not just the ticket.
* Build and run services across both stacks: TypeScript (Bun/Node, Prisma, Next.js) and Python (FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy).
* Own async \& event\-driven work — queues, streaming ingestion, scheduled jobs, retries, and idempotency. (A lot of our load never touches a request handler.)
* Ship LLM\-backed product features — tool calling, structured outputs, grounding against real data, and the failure handling that keeps them sane in front of users.
* Keep production legible — tracing, metrics, and alerts that fire only when action is needed. You own your deploys and their consequences.


**What You'll Bring**
* 5\+ years building and running backend systems in production. You've been on the hook when things broke.
* Dual\-stack proficiency: TypeScript/Node \+ Python — strong in one, genuinely productive in the other. This isn't a "Python nice\-to\-have" role.
* Relational databases at depth: Postgres or MySQL — schema design, migrations, indexing, and reading query plans to fix the slow ones.
* Streaming/event infrastructure in production: Kinesis or Kafka — producers, consumers, partitioning, replay, and handling backpressure and duplicates.
* Service design \& delivery — clean contracts, sensible boundaries, and knowing when not to split a service. Hands\-on with AWS, Docker, and CI/CD.
* End\-to\-end ownership — you've carried features from idea to production and lived with the results. Founding or product\-engineer experience is a huge plus.
* Engineering hygiene — writing tests with the change (not after), disciplined releases, and caring whether the metric actually moved.


**Preferred Experience**
* ML Platform: Serving models behind APIs, vector retrieval (pgvector/FAISS), feature pipelines, and model versioning/rollout. Keeping models alive in production counts double.
* LLM Application Engineering: Agent loops, tool calling, structured output, and evaluating output quality programmatically. Self\-hosted inference (vLLM, GPU serving, cost tuning) is a strong plus.
* Data at Scale: Redshift/BigQuery/Snowflake, and observability tools (OpenTelemetry, Datadog).
* Experimentation: A/B and shadow tests, guardrail metrics, and the discipline to read a flat result honestly.
* Domain Experience: Consumer social or dating products.


**What We Offer**
* Competitive pay along with an annual performance\-linked incentive (PLI).
* Employee benefits like Medical Insurance.
* Participation in Employee Phantom Grants Program (Stock Options).


**Life at Hunch**
 Hunch is a small team focused on shipping the parts of dating that usually stall \- getting two interested people into the same room.
   

  

**What We Hire For \- The ABCs**
 Most companies have a long list of values nobody remembers. We have three, and they show up in how we hire, what we ship, and how we talk about the work:
   

  

* Authenticity \- Real before polished. We build for real people on real first dates, and we hire the same way. No theater. If something's not working, say so; if it is, ship it.
* Boldness \- Dating got stuck because nobody wanted to break the pattern. We make the call on what to ship, what to cut, and what doesn't belong in the product, even when it's the harder choice.
* Curiosity \- The best people here ask a lot of small, useful questions — about users, about the data, about each other's work. We trust people who keep learning over people who already know.


**How We Work**
* Ownership, not theater \- You own outcomes, not status updates. Fewer meetings, fewer dashboards, more shipping.
* Flexibility that's real \- We care about the work, not the hours you sit at a desk. Take the afternoon, take the week \- show up for the stuff that matters.
* Move fast, don't burn out \- Hunch ships quickly because we cut the slow stuff, not because we work people into the ground. Velocity comes from focus, not from hours.
* Small team, big problems \- You'll work on things that matter to millions of people trying to actually meet someone. Every role moves the product.


**Backed by Global Investors**
 Hunch is backed by Hashed, AlphaWave, Brevan Howard and Polygon Studios.
   

  

**Experienced Leadership**
 Hunch is founded by a trio of industry veterans: Ish Goel (CEO), Nitika Goel (CPO), and Kartic Rakhra (CMO) \- serial entrepreneurs with their last exit from Nexus Mutual, a web3 consumer\-tech startup.

title: Market Engagement Manager, SheConnects Digital Accelerator
description:
**Location:** 
 Delhi
   

  

**Position type:** 
*Fixed Term Contract until March 31, 2028*
**What The Hiring Manager Says**
 “Working across India and Africa, this role is a great opportunity for someone with a strong commercial background who is also passionate about driving digital inclusion for underserved groups, especially women. As Market Engagement Manager, you will collaborate closely with partners to drive strategic interventions focused on increasing internet adoption and use. You’ll help create scalable and impactful solutions that can drive long\-term change for women and underserved populations.”
   

  

*Adrine Muhura – Senior Market Engagement Manager, M4D*
**About The Team**
 GSMA Mobile for Development (M4D) is a dedicated global team within the GSMA, which brings together our mobile operator members, tech innovators, the development community and governments, to realise the impact of mobile in low\- and middle\-income countries:
   

  

 This role is part of he SheConnects Digital Accelerator which was founded by the Reliance Foundation and Gates Foundation to advance women’s digital inclusion. The Accelerator aims to scale proven, high\-impact solutions that enable women and girls to participate fully in the digital world, improving their lives and livelihoods. The Accelerator grants are supported by Reliance Foundation in India and by Gates Foundation in Sub Saharan Africa. By catalysing innovative partnerships and use cases, the Accelerator will strengthen evidence on what works, foster south\-to\-south learning, and help shape a more inclusive global digital ecosystem.
   

  

**About The Role**
 You will work as part of the team to support the scale up of approaches to increase women’s adoption and use of the internet, reducing the gender gap.
   

  

 Key responsibilities include working as part of a team to:
   

  

- Support a portfolio of partners across Africa and India interested in accelerating women’s adoption and use of the internet, with a particular focus on increasing smartphone ownership and use. This will include managing and delivering technical assistance and advisory support to organisations being supported by the initiative to help drive and scale impactful in\-country actions. This includes:

* Ensuring effective contracting and management of packages of technical assistance and provisioning strategic advisory support.
* Providing thought leadership, analysing market opportunities, inputting to the design and delivery of propositions, creating and delivering strategy workshops for partners, and tracking both commercial and social outcomes.
* Generate and share key insights which drive increased awareness and action among stakeholders as well as supporting knowledge exchange between partners. This includes documenting insights and learnings and sharing your findings with the industry ecosystem through presentations, case studies, toolkits, blogs, events and meetings with relevant stakeholders.


**About You**
 You will have a strong commercial experience, gained through working as a management consultant or within corporate strategy, business planning or marketing functions, ideally within or for the digital sector.
   

  

 You have familiarity with strategies that drive inclusion for underserved communities, including women. This will ideally include knowledge and understanding of approaches to improving handset affordability and adoption.
   

  

 You can quickly understand new data and business models to identify commercial opportunities that can also have a substantial social impact when successfully scaled.
   

  

 You will be confident and comfortable presenting to and engaging with senior leadership in the private sector, quick to identify insights and summarise key points.
   

  

 You are compelling and persuasive and can draw on GSMA and other insights to add value to partners and provide evidence to drive sustainable action.
   

  

 You have strong verbal and written communication skills and can document insights and learnings to share your findings with the industry ecosystem
   

  

 You are a strong team player, self\-aware and able to work collaboratively by default, supporting others and knowing when to reach out for support yourself.
   

  

 You have strong project management skills and organised to deliver high impact outputs.
   

  

 You will be passionate about the transformative potential of the internet and digital services to improve women’s livelihoods, economic security and resilience.
   

  

**About Your Skills**
**Communication** 
 – Critical for influence, credibility, and impact. This role requires the ability to distil market insights, data, and partner learnings into clear, compelling narratives that resonate with senior decision\-makers across the private sector, governments, donors, and the broader digital inclusion ecosystem. Strong written and verbal communication and thought leadership that shape industry discourse and drive action.
   

  

**Delivery** 
 – Essential for translating strategy into execution. The role demands strong project and delivery management skills to oversee multiple workstreams simultaneously, ensure effective contracting and management of technical assistance, and deliver high\-impact outputs on time and to quality. Delivery capability ensures that partner engagements result in tangible commercial and social outcomes.
   

  

**Influence** 
 – Central to driving behaviour change and sustainable action among diverse stakeholders. This skill enables the role to persuade and align senior leaders within mobile operators, ecosystem partners, and GSMA internal teams around evidence\-based recommendations. Influence is critical to positioning insights as actionable, building momentum for scale, and embedding strategies to advance women's digital inclusion.
   

  

**Stakeholder Management** 
 – Fundamental to the success of the program. This role requires the ability to build, manage, and maintain trusted relationships with senior executives, mobile operators, enabling organisations, donors, and internal teams. Effective stakeholder management supports collaboration across geographies and sectors, balances differing incentives, and ensures alignment between commercial objectives and inclusion goals.
   

  

**Commercial Awareness** 
 – Strong commercial acumen enables the identification of market opportunities that can drive both business value and social impact, particularly in areas such as smartphone affordability, adoption, and usage. This skill ensures that recommendations are grounded in realistic business models, market dynamics, and partner priorities, strengthening the credibility and long\-term sustainability of digital interventions.
   

  

**Contract type**
 Fixed Term Contract (Fixed Term)
   

  

**Worker type**
 Employee
   

  

**What We Offer**
 Working at the GSMA offers you unparalleled access to the mobile industry. We offer a chance to truly shape the direction of mobile, whatever your role. By joining the GSMA, you will be exposed to a fast\-paced rapidly evolving environment, working on global solutions, genuinely fascinating and industry\-changing projects and a stimulating and dynamic environment designed to enable you to flourish.
   

  

 In addition to architect\-designed offices and competitive compensation, our benefits include fantastic learning \& development opportunities, generous holiday allowances, four additional days off for professional development and many others.
   

  

 To learn more about the GSMA, visit our career site, our LinkedIn page and our Twitter page.
   

  

 Being You at the GSMA
   

  

 We care deeply about diversity, equity and inclusivity and aspire to be the best at it. Your well\-being and work/life balance is important, so flexi\-time and remote working is available to all staff. We're keen to ensure everyone is equal, represented and connected so we particularly encourage applications from all demographics. The sucess of the GSMA year on year will continue to be contributed by people from all walks of life.
   

  

**GSMA Values**
 Our values not only drive our culture – they shape how we work and interact inside and outside our global organisation.
   

  

**Passionately driven**
 We approach everything we do with unparalleled capability, tenacity and commitment, knowing that the challenging scale, pace and complexity of our work is what leads to its world\-changing impact.
   

  

**Insightful leaders**
 We continually develop and engage our expertise, insight and creativity so that we’re always ready to respond to the changing landscape with authority, agility and nuance.
   

  

**Stronger together**
 We lean on each other so the industry can lean on us, embracing our diversity by actively seeking out perspectives and skill sets beyond our own, fuelling each other’s successes and constantly asking how we can help.
   

  

 Underpinning our values is our collective mindset to show up purposefully as good human beings every day, in every situation. When we’re at our best – we are collaborative, considerate and compassionate to others, and we create a safe space for one another to thrive, assuming positive intent in our colleagues. And if we aren’t at our best and the pressure is on – we feel free to be ourselves but still remain curious, lean into the tough stuff and we are always respectful to others and accountable for the part we play.

title: Deputy Chief Financial Officer, Trilogy (Remote) - $1,600,000/year USD
description:
Most finance executives inherit a system. You will redesign one, then decide where the capital goes.
   

  

 Trilogy is looking for the executive who can turn a portfolio of businesses into a capital allocation system: continuously ranking where the next dollar should go, backing those decisions with rigorous models, and moving capital toward its highest\-return uses. You will own the calls that matter: fund or kill a business line; invest or hold; acquire or walk away; refinance or pay down debt. Every recommendation must connect strategy to cash, liquidity, covenants, risk, and enterprise value.
   

  

 Just as important, you will architect an AI\-native finance function built to scale without decision bottlenecks. This does not mean sprinkling AI tools onto a traditional finance organization. You will redesign reporting, planning, controls, portfolio monitoring, and decision support around what AI and automation can now do. You won't need to personally build every workflow, but you must use AI deeply enough to know its edges: where it accelerates analysis, where it fails, and where expert judgment must take over. The result should be a smaller, more senior, higher\-leverage finance organization rather than a growing pyramid of people and processes.
   

  

 You will operate directly with Trilogy's CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners, with personal accountability for the financial truth behind major decisions. As Deputy CFO, this is a $1\.6M/year W\-2 salaried role for someone who has already earned credibility at serious financial scale and now wants the mandate to compound enterprise value across an entire portfolio. If you want your impact measured by the quality of your capital decisions and the financial system you leave behind, apply.
   

  

**What You Will Be Doing**
* Allocating capital across the portfolio: Run capital and portfolio reviews, rank competing uses of capital on risk\-adjusted return, and make clear fund, hold, restructure, exit, debt\-paydown, or acquisition recommendations.
* Architecting an AI\-native finance system: Redesign planning, reporting, consolidation, controls, portfolio monitoring, and financial workflows around AI, automation, and scalable systems rather than additional headcount.
* Driving investments and transactions: Build and defend the financial case for strategic investments, M\&A, financing, and refinancing, including integrated models, downside scenarios, capital structure, covenant implications, and execution plans.
* Owning board and capital\-partner communication: Give the CEO, board, lenders, and capital partners fast, quantified, defensible truth, with recommendations that make the decision and trade\-offs explicit.
* Building a high\-leverage finance leadership team: Set the bar for a small group of exceptional finance leaders while creating systems that allow new ventures and greater complexity to be absorbed without linear organizational growth.


**What You Won’t Be Doing**
* Running finance as a reporting factory. Closing the books and producing audit workpapers are the Controller's responsibilities. Your job is to turn financial information into better capital decisions.
* Building a large finance organization to handle complexity. Scale should come from better systems, AI leverage, automation, and exceptional people, not layers of management.
* Adding AI as a superficial productivity tool. You will architect workflows around its real capabilities and limitations, which requires substantial firsthand use.
* Producing strategy decks without financial consequences. Major recommendations must carry the integrated model, downside case, capital implications, and execution guardrails behind them.
* Managing the board through narrative. The numbers, assumptions, risks, and recommended action should be clear enough to withstand scrutiny.


**Deputy Chief Financial Officer Key Responsibilities**
 Build a durable, AI\-native finance function that compounds enterprise value across Trilogy's portfolio by allocating capital to its highest\-return uses and creating financial systems and controls that scale without decision bottlenecks.
   

  

**Basic Requirements**
* Experience as the most senior finance decision\-maker, or their direct deputy, for a business or portfolio with $100M\+ in annual revenue across multiple legal entities.
* Personal ownership of major capital\-allocation decisions, including the ability to explain what was funded, reduced, or rejected; the dollars involved; the trade\-offs; and your recommendation.
* Decision ownership on at least one $25M\+ closed M\&A, financing, or refinancing transaction, with direct responsibility for negotiation, financing selection, board recommendation, or post\-close integration.
* Direct experience presenting to and taking live questions from a board of directors.
* Ownership of an external audit relationship under US GAAP or IFRS, directly or through a Controller reporting to you.
* Hands\-on experience with a true enterprise ERP such as SAP, NetSuite, Oracle, Workday, or equivalent.
* Recent experience re\-architecting a finance workflow around AI, with enough regular personal AI use to understand where the technology is reliable, where it is not, and how those boundaries should shape finance\-system design.
* Ability to operate integrated 3\-statement models and defend assumptions, downside scenarios, covenant math, capital structure, and recommendations under live questioning.
* Strong written and verbal English, with experience communicating directly with CEOs, boards, lenders, or capital partners.
* Located within the UTC−8 to UTC\+3 time\-zone range.


**Nice\-to\-have Requirements**
* CPA, ACA, ACCA, CIMA, CFA, MBA, or comparable finance credential.
* Earlier career experience in private equity, investment banking, M\&A, corporate finance, or another environment requiring rigorous modeling and high\-stakes capital decisions.
* Experience rebuilding a finance function rather than simply inheriting and operating one.
* Experience across a portfolio, multi\-entity, or PE\-backed operating environment.


**About Trilogy**
 Hundreds of software businesses run on the Trilogy Business Platform. For three decades, Trilogy has been known for 3 things: Relentlessly seeking top talent, innovating new technology, and incubating new businesses.
   

  

 Our technological innovation is spearheaded by a passion for simple customer\-facing designs. Our incubation of new businesses ranges from entirely new moon\-shot ideas to rearchitecting existing projects for today's modern cloud\-based stack.
   

  

 Trilogy is a place where you can be surrounded with great people, be proud of doing great work, and grow your career in leaps and bounds.
   

  

 There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!
   

  

**Working with us**
 This is a full\-time (40 hours per week), long\-term position. The position is immediately available and requires entering into an independent contractor agreement with Crossover as a Contractor of Record. The compensation level for this role is $800 USD/hour, which equates to $1,600,000 USD/year assuming 40 hours per week and 50 weeks per year. The payment period is weekly. Consult www.crossover.com/help\-and\-faqs for more details on this topic.

title: AI Integration Engineer – Digital Transformation (m/f/d)
description:
At Flix, we offer a dynamic work environment with competitive pay, strong growth opportunities, and a tech\-driven approach to making travel more accessible, sustainable, and affordable.
   

  

 Joining the People \& Organization Digital Transformation team, you will work directly with the Head of Digital Transformation and a close\-knit team of four engineers based in Berlin. Your work will span automation engineering, AI application deployment on top of HR systems — with direct impact on how Flix manages its people technology globally. Are you an engineer who knows how to turn AI ideas into real\-world applications—deploying Claude\-based solutions, building integrations, and putting the right security and governance in place? If you’ve built innovative AI products, like those emerging from HR AI Day and beyond, and have the engineering mindset to take them from idea to scalable solution, we’d love to hear from you.
   

  

 This is a pure technical role. There is no administrative overhead, no time\-critical firefighting and no expectation of HR domain expertise on day one — we can teach you the domain. This is an exciting, problem\-solving\-focused role at the intersection of AI, automation, and HR solution architecture. While the technical skills can be developed, what we cannot teach is the engineering mindset, depth of integration expertise, and natural instinct for automation that this role demands.
   

  

 This is a hybrid role based in Gurugram OR Bangalore with a minimum office presence of 3 days per week. The role has a Europe and APAC\-facing scope, with regular collaboration across Central European time zones.
   

  

**About The Role**
* Lead the technical workstream supporting internal automation projects —evaluating global HR system options, assessing integration complexity, mapping data dependencies and supporting potential migration execution from Workday or equivalent enterprise HR platforms.
* Design and build automation and integration workflows using n8n,UiPath and Python — including multi\-step orchestration, exception handling, retries, monitoring, alerting and structured documentation.
* Build and maintain enterprise system integrations using REST APIs,OAuth 2\.0, webhooks, SFTP and event\-driven patterns across the HR technology landscape.
* Develop secure AI integrations connecting platforms such as Claude with HRIS and enterprise systems using MCP servers, connectors, plugins and agent frameworks — with appropriate access controls and user\-level permissions.
* Deploy and operate internal applications and AI\-powered tools on Flix's hosting infrastructure (AWS), including RBAC/ABAC access models, secrets management, credential rotation and audit logging.
* Analyse business processes end\-to\-end, identify automation opportunities and design scalable target\-state architectures that can support both the evaluation phase and eventual migration or implementation execution.
* Engage with cross\-functional stakeholders across Europe and APAC —translating complex technical requirements into clear solution designs and project deliverables across 3–6 month project scopes.


**About You**
* 6–7\+ years of hands\-on professional experience in automation engineering, systems integration, solution architecture or AI application development. Exceptional mid\-level candidates with strong technical depth will also be considered.
* Demonstrable experience building and delivering automation workflows and enterprise integrations — this is an engineering role, not a data analytics or reporting role. Experience in Python, n8n and UiPath is essential.
* Strong working knowledge of API design and integration patterns —REST APIs, OAuth 2\.0, webhooks, SFTP and event\-driven architectures.
* Hands\-on experience deploying and operating applications on AWS,including Lambda, API Gateway, Bedrock, Glue, Secrets Manager and CI/CD pipeline management.
* Solid software engineering fundamentals — Git/GitHub, Docker,structured release management and familiarity with security practices including least privilege, RBAC/ABAC and credential handling.
* Experience with Workday or enterprise HRIS platforms (configuration, integration or migration) is a strong advantage and a meaningful differentiator — though not an absolute requirement if your automation and integration fundamentals are strong.
* Comfort working across European and APAC time zones, collaborating with a Berlin\-based team and contributing to strategic cross\-functional initiatives.
* n8n Level 1 or Level 2 certification is strongly preferred.


 We recognize that everyone carries a unique set of valuable skills and experiences. If you think you could have an impact even though you don't meet 100% of the requirements, we still encourage you to apply. We want to hear from you!
   

  

**What We Offer**
* Travel perks: 12 free Flix vouchers \+ 12 discount vouchers for friends \& family.
* Work from (M)Anywhere: Depending on your role, work from another location for up to 60 days per year.
* Hybrid work model: We are an office\-first company, but we offer flexibility to balance work and life.
* Wellbeing support: Access confidential 1:1 counselling, courses, and stress management for yourself and up to four family members.
* Learning \& Development: Take advantage of language classes, training courses, and expert\-led sessions to grow your skills.
* Mentoring Program: Connect with experienced colleagues to gain insights and accelerate your career.


 To view more local benefits specific to each office location, please check out this link: Locations \- Flix Career
   

  

**Why Join Flix?**
 At Flix, you’ll find teams that rally together to overcome challenges and spark creativity. We believe in ownership culture \- giving you the freedom to take initiative, make an impact, and shape your own career path.
   

  

 As we continue to expand across the globe, you can make a real difference in how we work.
   

  

 If you’re ready to grow and lead your journey, Flix is the place for you!

title: Evidence Lead, AI Access Initiative (EAII Advisors)
description:
**About The AI Access Initiative (2AI)**
 We're at an inflection point in artificial intelligence \- presenting both tremendous potential opportunity and risk for people in developing countries. AI capabilities are improving on a timescale measured in months, while development systems often move on timescales measured in decades. Much of the technology needed for positive impact exists today, but few organizations exist to bridge research, deployment, and scaled implementation: we must act now to ensure AI's benefits reach people in poverty in LMICs.
   

  

 Incubated at Evidence Action, we're scaling The AI Access Initiative, an organization focused on scaling AI\-enabled 'big bets' to benefit tens or hundreds of millions of people in poverty in low\- and middle\-income countries (LMICs). We operate at the intersection of global development actors, top AI labs, and leading researchers to drive meaningful access to AI's benefits for the 3\.5 billion people living in poverty globally. We create "public good," open\-sourced playbooks, toolkits, and insights that define how to design and launch tractable and impactful AI\-enabled programs. Given the scale of opportunity, we expect our portfolio to expand substantially, but to start, we're scaling two programs focused on AI in Agriculture and AI in Health.
   

  

* Agriculture: We have an ambitious goal to reach 100M\+ farmers with AI\-enabled weather forecasts, expand forecast R\&D to generate novel forecasts, and build public and private sector (WhatsApp, telcos) delivery channels to deliver new, LLM\-generated voice and image content that maximizes behavior change.
* Health: Here, our initial goal is to scale AI\-enabled clinical decision support to 20M\+ people via telemedicine platforms, dramatically improving diagnosis and health outcomes at a national level. We are also planning to explore and test novel interventions for low\-resource settings, including direct\-to\-consumer (DTC) health interventions.


 We are led by former Evidence Action CEO Kanika Bahl, a founding member of Anthropic's Long\-Term Benefit Trust, and advised by Nobel Laureate Michael Kremer; Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic; and Kent Walker, President, Global Affairs for Alphabet and Google. This work builds on Evidence Action's track record reaching 530M\+ people with cost\-effective, evidence\-based programs across 9 countries in Africa and Asia, with a focus on last\-mile delivery.
   

  

**About 2AI India And EAII Advisors**
 EAII Advisors, Evidence Action's technical partner in India, supports state governments in delivering evidence\-based public health programs. Operating across 10 states, EAII Advisors provides technical assistance to ministries of health, education, water, and women and child development, reducing health burdens in impoverished communities and improving the long\-term wellbeing of children and families.
   

  

 2AI India is being incubated as a project within EAII Advisors, with plans to spin off into an independent entity at the end of this year. We are hiring a founding team: the first hires will shape the culture, establish the operating model, and own early wins before the organization scales.
   

  

**Roles And Responsibilities**
 The Evidence Lead is 2AI India's primary engine for measuring whether our programs work and why. This is not a traditional monitoring and evaluation (M\&E) role. The focus is generating insights that change program design in real time. Data collection for government reporting is a real but secondary function, roughly 20% of the role. The Evidence Lead is also expected to be actively applying AI and machine learning (ML) tools to evaluation.
   

  

*Evidence Generation and Program Measurement*
* Measures the effectiveness of new programs and ideas, from early concept tests through scaled delivery, and defines what "working" means for each before it launches
* Identifies the right data sources for evaluation, including administrative data, program data, partner data, and primary collection, and making the tradeoffs between rigor, cost, and speed explicit
* Designs and runs cost\-effectiveness models, making the assumptions behind each result legible to the people making the call
* Builds the measurement and feedback loops into program design from the start rather than retrofitting them after launch
* Owns the data collection and reporting obligations that come with government partnerships, roughly 20% of the role,


*Thought Partnership to Programs*
* Serves as a thought partner to the programs team on program design, ensuring programs are built to be measurable and monitoring and evaluation efforts measure what really matters.
* Translates findings into recommendations that program leads can act on, and is explicit about the confidence behind each one


*AI and ML Applied to Evaluation*
* Applies AI and ML tools directly to evaluation and data analysis work, and keeps that practice current as the tools change
* Builds the data and modeling infrastructure that lets a small team run rapid and purpose\-built analysis


*External Representation*
* Presents 2AI's evidence and data externally, with findings tailored to the needs of specific audiences: funders, partners, government counterparts, and the research community


*Team building and enablement*
* Fosters a strong, values\-aligned culture as a leader across the organization
* Willingness to roll\-up sleeves and pitch in to the organization building activities required of a founding team
* Overtime, hires and enables a team of strong monitoring, learning, and evaluation professionals committed to objectively assessing our programs and fostering their improvement


 Disclaimer: The duties and responsibilities described are not a comprehensive list and additional tasks may be assigned to the employee from time to time.
   

  

**Requirements**
**Essentials:**
* Relevant professional background: 7\-9 years of experience in M\&E, impact evaluation, or applied research in global health or international development
* Rigorous evidence environment: has worked in an organization where methodological standards were high and contested, such as academic research, a think tank, or an equivalent research lab
* Applied AI and ML fluency: is already using AI and ML tools in evaluation and data analysis work today
* Cost\-effectiveness modelling: experience building and updating cost\-effectiveness analyses, and can explain the assumptions driving a result to a non\-technical decision\-maker
* Analytical structuring: structures ambiguous problems, thinks analytically, and solves quantitative problems without waiting for a fully specified brief
* Program collaboration instincts: experience working in close proximity to programs; can understand how program needs and constraints differ from research needs, and adjusts the evidence agenda accordingly
* Clear communication: shows clarity of thought, writes compellingly, and translates technical information into common language for varied audiences
* External credibility: can present to funders, government counterparts, and technical peers and hold up under questioning
* Experience navigating Indian government data systems and state\-level reporting requirements
* Comfort with ambiguity: a track record of doing well in early\-stage, resource\-constrained environments where the path is not defined and you build it as you go
* Initiative and bias to action: takes ownership of unassigned problems and moves without being asked


**What Success Looks Like**
 In the First 6 Months:
   

  

* You have a working measurement approach with key indicators for the agriculture program, agreed with the Program Director, that specifies what evidence would change the program's direction
* You have built or adapted a cost\-effectiveness model for at least one priority intervention, and leadership understands and trusts its assumptions
* You have mapped the available data landscape in India, including what government and partner systems can and cannot tell us


**Compensation :** 
 Competitive and commensurate with the individual's credentials, experience, and previous pay scale.
   

  

**Benefits**
 EAII provides a comprehensive benefits package for employees. Benefits include:
   

  

* Comprehensive health insurance with IPD and OPD provisions
* Life and Accidental insurance
* PF, ESIC and Gratuity as per statutory requirements
* Generous leave
* Mental and physical wellbeing benefits
* Learning \& Development benefits
* Avenues for engagement and recognition


 Note: This role will be open for applications until October 09,2026 . Please apply at your earliest convenience. We may close this search earlier than the specified date if we find the right fit. Due to the volume of applications received, we will only be able to contact shortlisted candidates.

title: Central Monitor
description:
**Job Title: Central Monitor** 




**Location: Gurugram, India** 




**Reports to: Associate Director, Clinical Trial Management** 




  





*Help IAVI translate science into global health impact as a Central Monitor!* 




*IAVI is seeking a Central Monitor in India, who will be responsible for leading and supporting centralized monitoring and risk\-based monitoring activities for IAVI\-sponsored clinical trials. This role will closely work with the global Clinical Trial Managers (CTMs) and cross\-functional study team members to support ongoing, data\-driven oversight of study and site risks.* 




  





**Key Responsibilities:** 



* Lead risk\-based and central monitoring activities for assigned IAVI\-sponsored clinical trials in accordance with the Monitoring Plan, Risk Management Plan and other study\-specific plans. This may include but not limited to:
* Conduct ongoing review and analysis of clinical trial data listings as defined in the Monitoring Plan to identify missing or inconsistent data, data outliers, unusual trends or distributions, potential protocol deviations, data quality concerns, safety signals and site performance issues.
* Track the status of site KRIs and other risk indicators defined in the Risk Management Plan and assess changes or trends over time.
* Integrate findings from KRI review, data\-listing analysis and other relevant study information to assess site and overall study risk.
* Coordinate and lead central monitoring review meetings as per frequency defined in the Monitoring Plan.
* Prepare and maintain Central Monitoring Reports documenting the results of central monitoring activities, identified risks, trends, findings and recommended actions.
* Work with the Clinical Trial Manager and relevant functional teams to investigate identified issues, understand potential root causes and determine appropriate and actionable follow\-up.
* Escalate potential concerns and other significant or critical findings to the appropriate study team members, where appropriate.
* Lead or support identification of appropriate risk mitigation actions, including recommendations for targeted site follow\-up or changes to monitoring approaches, as appropriate.
* Support the study team during study planning and start\-up in identifying Critical\-to\-Quality factors, key risks, acceptable ranges and KRIs, as appropriate.
* Provide input into the central monitoring approach and relevant sections of the Monitoring Plan and Risk Management Plan.
* Provide central monitoring insights and study risk updates to the clinical operations and broader study team, as relevant.
* Contribute to review of study status, site performance and other operational metrics as appropriate.
* Support preparation of study updates, presentations and other materials related to clinical operations and risk management.
* Participate in Clinical Operations departmental activities, including refinement/review of tools, templates and processes for central monitoring and risk\-based quality management.



  





**Education and Work Experience:** 



* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific or related field is required.
* Minimum 5 years of clinical trials experience including clinical monitoring is required, preferably including clinical monitoring, clinical trial management, clinical data management or other relevant clinical research experience.
* Experience with centralized monitoring and/or risk\-based quality management (RBQM) is strongly preferred.
* Experience supporting multinational or global clinical trials, preferably in sponsor, CRO, or public health settings, is desirable.



  





**Qualifications and Skills:** 



* Excellent knowledge of ICH GCP as well as the Declaration of Helsinki and relevant country specific regulations are required.
* Good understanding of Risk\-Based Quality Management principles.
* Interpersonal skills and ability to work effectively in a cooperative and collaborative manner with all levels, and across functional teams is required.
* Strong analytical and critical\-thinking skills and ability to interpret clinical and operational data from multiple sources.
* Ability to work on problems of moderate complexity and diverse scope using good judgment within defined procedures and policies to determine appropriate action is required.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills are required.
* Ability to work independently and exercise sound judgment in identifying and escalating risks.
* A professional demeanor, as well as a pleasant manner and positive “can\-do” attitude.
* Flexible and adaptable to accommodate changing deadlines to meet organizational needs is required.
* Excellent computer skills and proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel is required.
* Experience with centralized monitoring platforms, dashboards or data visualization tools such as Power BI or equivalent would be a plus.
* High level of independence in performing responsibilities is highly desirable.
* Familiarity with HIV, TB, emerging infectious diseases
* Ability and willingness to collaborate effectively across time zones and geographic locations is required.



  





**Organizational Overview:** 




 IAVI is a nonprofit scientific research organization dedicated to addressing urgent, unmet global health challenges including HIV and tuberculosis. Our mission is to translate scientific discoveries into affordable, globally accessible public health solutions. Through scientific and clinical research in Africa, India, Europe, and the U.S., IAVI is pioneering the development of biomedical innovations designed for broad global access. We develop vaccines and antibodies in and for the developing world and seek to accelerate their introduction in low\-income countries. IAVI programs and partnerships are grounded in the regions of the world where the disease burden is the greatest, and our approach emphasizes sustainability. Our network of clinical research center partners in Africa and India helps strengthen in\-country research capacity and supports the training and education of the next generation of scientists. The global impact of our science includes fundamental contributions to understanding the biology of HIV infection, which IAVI and others are applying toward advancing vaccine science and immunology. IAVI accelerates scientific discovery and development by fostering unique collaborations among academia, industry, local communities, governments, and funders to explore new and better ways to address public health threats that disproportionately affect people living in poverty. Our global reach, including a clinical research network in five countries in sub\-Saharan Africa and in India, has allowed us to make fundamental contributions to understanding the epidemiology, transmission, virology, and immunology of HIV. This work played a key role in facilitating the design of promising HIV vaccine candidates, as well as the discovery of broadly neutralizing antibodies that are now being advanced as promising approaches for HIV prevention. Our integrated capabilities in vaccine and antibody discovery, development, and clinical research take advantage of bio\-pharmaceutical industry expertise to accelerate the development and testing of prevention methods for HIV and other diseases. Through the Product Development Center, we support external researchers with technical and scientific expertise to accelerate the development of their own products.
 




  





**IAVI CORE VALUES:** 



* Commitment: We deliver on our mission, proactively transforming promises into tangible results
* Stewardship: We steward IAVI's resources responsibly to ensure IAVI's long\-term success and global health impact
* Integrity: We uphold strong moral principles to maintain our credibility as a nonprofit scientific research organization
* Collaboration: We work as one IAVI team and partner with others to deliver globally accessible, urgently needed, public health solutions



  





 Disclaimer: Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities and skills required of personnel so classified. This document does not create an employment contract, implied or otherwise, other than an “at\-will” relationship. IAVI is an equal opportunity employer and applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

It is IAVI’s policy to provide equal opportunity without regard to race, citizenship, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, height, weight, disability (including physical and mental conditions unrelated to job performance), religion, creed, caste, home language, ancestry, national origin, pregnancy, marital or partnership status, sexual orientation, status as a protected veteran, ethnicity, genetic information, predisposing genetic characteristic, status as a victim of domestic violence, stalking and sex offenses, HIV status, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws.

description:

* Automation Mastery: Build and maintain automated deployment pipelines using Ansible and GitOps principles to ensure repeatable, production\-ready environments.

title: Manager Impact, India and Southeast Asia

description:
The Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (Global Energy Alliance) The Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet (Global Energy Alliance) works for a world where everyone has access to affordable, reliable, clean electricity and the means to use it to improve their lives. Our Alliance builds transformative public, private, philanthropic partnerships to end energy poverty and accelerate green economic opportunity. Founded in 2021 by The Rockefeller Foundation, IKEA Foundation, and Bezos Earth Fund, we design innovative projects/programs, unlock finance, strengthen institutions and transform markets, delivering progress anchored in deep community engagement. By uniting actors across the value chain, from households to heads of state, we go beyond individual projects to drive lasting systems change. With work in more than 30 countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, our Alliance aims to reach 1 billion people with clean electricity, prevent 4 billion tons of carbon emissions and create or improve 150 million jobs.
   

  

**Contract type: Fulltime, Open ended**
**Reports Directly To**
 Direct Reports:
   

  

**Matrix/Dual Reports**
 Chief Impact Officer
   

  

 None
   

  

 VP, India; MD, Grids of the Future
   

  

**Overview Of The Role**
 Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet’s goals are bold and audacious. We recognize that the path to a just energy transition worldwide will be complex, non\-linear, and filled with successes and opportunities, alongside failures and challenges. The Manager, Impact, India and Southeast Asia will support our effort to measure our contribution to impact through evaluations, monitoring and learning. Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) is embedded within our operating model, to ensure that we have an ear to the ground so we remain responsive and opportunistic, while generating insights that support continuous improvement.
   

  

 Stepping into a start\-up environment, the Manager, Impact, India and Southeast Asia will lead monitoring, evaluation and learning for the India and Southeast Asia portfolio, guided by the organization’s Impact framework. They will also lead impact measurement for the Grids of the Future pillar across all regions, and provide monitoring and analytics support across the global portfolio. They will be responsible for independently establishing the routine and long\-term work component of these workstreams, ensuring that they are efficiently managed and executed.
   

  

**Accountabilities** 
  

  

* 
+ Monitoring: Providing backend impact data quality assurance for all India and Southeast Asia transactions. Provide technical advice on target setting, indicators, theory of change mechanisms, causality links for the India and Southeast Asia portfolio. Onboard and train program teams on results monitoring sheets – ensuring compliance. They will also support the monitoring function across the global portfolio, including data compilation, quality checks and analytics for quarterly impact reporting, working alongside the Alliance’s external monitoring and learning partner.
+ Grids of the Future impact: Leading impact measurement for the Grids of the Future pillar across all regions. Developing and maintaining expected\-impact estimates for utility partnerships, grid digitalization, battery energy storage and distributed energy resource programs, working with program teams and external modelling partners. Tracking realized impact against expected impact as programs move through the pipeline, and designing evaluations of utility\-level outcomes such as reliability, losses and effects on consumers.
+ Evaluation: Sourcing and managing independent evaluation partners working closely with the Director of Evaluation. Establishing the pulse on what needs evaluation and when by closely working with the India and Southeast Asia and Grids of the Future teams in sourcing evaluation questions. Selecting fit for purpose evaluation approaches and tools and sense checking their design and functionality.
+ Learning: Support the team in designing and managing ongoing reflection, sense\-making, and learning from the work to inform potential shifts in strategy when necessary, using data and evidence to rationalize change.
+ Capacity building: Onboarding, training and operationalizing Impact functions in country teams, solution teams and hiring monitoring evaluation and learning consultants. Ensuring that all requirements per the Impact framework are met in the investment cycle for all India and Southeast Asia programs.
+ Systems integration: Ensuring the internal Global Energy Alliance systems tracking progress on program implementation, financial execution and impact measuring are integrating, working in close collaboration with the IT systems manager, the management teams for country programs and scalable solutions and the Investment team.
+ Advisory function: Advising global Impact colleagues and external technical providers by ground truthing India and Southeast Asia portfolio realities.


**BEHAVIORAL COMPETENCIES**
**Preferred Attributes**
* Working in Partnership: Learning with, learning from, and learning for our partners, particularly those who are closest to the work on the ground. Balancing the needs of multiple stakeholders and working in partnership wherever possible.
* Directs Work: Being strategic with efforts and generating information that informs decision making and improves impact. Providing direction and removing obstacles to get work done.
* Manages Complexity: Makes sense of complex, high quantity, and sometimes contradictory information to effectively solve problems.
* Values Differences: Recognizes the value of different perspectives and commits to inclusion, equity, and diversity in every aspect of work.
* Intellectual Humility: We know that we don’t have all the answer. We strive to be equally comfortable talking about what is not working as we are celebrating our successes. We listen to the voices of those we serve.
* Innovation and Entrepreneurial Spirit: A self\-starter who takes initiative to identify areas of improvement and uses an energetic, pragmatic, and creative approach to optimize practice; embodying ‘Start\-Up Philosophy.’


**Required Experience**
* 10\-15 years of experience in monitoring, evaluation, and learning.
* Advanced degree in relevant subjects such as economics, public policy, or similar areas with strong training in evaluation, monitoring and learning.
* Experience in developing best\-in\-class monitoring, evaluation and learning approaches including designing and establishing these systems from scratch. Ideal experience gained in a complex organizational environment.
* Substantial experience of monitoring, evaluation and learning in the context of climate and energy programs, and/or programs driving systems change. Experience with contribution analysis will be a plus.
* Experience measuring the impact of grid infrastructure, utility performance or battery energy storage programs, including modelling expected impacts and validating them against realized results.
* Experience working in India and Southeast Asia, with familiarity with the region’s energy sector, utilities and government programs.
* Experience working independently in a fast\-paced environment.
* Experience working with contractors, consultants to ensure value for money and quality actionable outcomes.
* Exceptional attention to detail.
* Strong writing skills.
* Expertise in STATA, R or similar software packages, and MS Excel.
* Experience with Power BI or other dashboard tools, data engineering and applied use of AI tools for analysis will be a plus.


 Please submit your application on or before
 **2 October COB.** 
 The Global Energy Alliance reserves the right to close the job advert early if we receive a high number of suitable applications.
   

  

*We operate from a strong commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion in everything we do. It is not only the right thing to do – we could not make an impact without our team members' diverse perspectives and experiences. We expect all Global Energy Alliance employees to contribute by developing their unique perspectives and talent, challenging conventional wisdom through evidence and reason, and amplifying marginalized voices.* 
  

  

*Global Energy Alliance is committed to the principles of equal employment opportunity and compliance with all federal, state, and local laws concerning employment discrimination, including the Americans with Disabilities Act. To this end, the organization ensures equal opportunity to all employees and applicants regardless of race, color, age, gender, sexual orientation, religion, marital status, national origin or ancestry, citizenship, lawful alien status, physical, mental, and medical disability, veteran status, or liability for service in the United States Armed Forces.* 
  

  

**Global Energy Alliance is an Equal Opportunity Employer.**

title: Community & Growth Freelancer
description:
Last updated: 15 September 2026
   

  

 Jump to section
   

  

 About The Role
   

  

 What you will do
   

  

**What Success Looks Like — And How We Grow**
 Who might be right for this
   

  

 Working arrangement and how to apply
   

  

**About The Role**
 KindVoice connects Seekers — people who want someone to talk to — with volunteer Listeners through private voice conversations. The platform is built. We now need help finding our first communities and learning what makes people trust, try and return to it.
   

  

 This is not a conventional social\-media role. We are looking for a community builder, not someone focused on content calendars or impressions: a person who discovers what works through conversations and practical experiments.
   

  

 You will work directly with the founder and have considerable freedom to test ideas, share honest feedback and help shape our approach.
   

  

 What you will do
   

  

 You will find places where potential Seekers and Listeners already spend their time and identify respectful ways to introduce KindVoice.
   

* Find and engage potential volunteer Listeners.
* Introduce a manageable number of new Seekers to KindVoice.
* Build relationships with community organizers and potential partners.
* Establish and develop appropriate KindVoice social and community channels.
* Talk with early users and gather honest feedback.
* Test different communities, messages and acquisition approaches.
* Identify problems with our messaging, onboarding or user experience and turn successful experiments into repeatable practices.


 You will have a short weekly conversation with the founder to discuss what happened, what you learned and what we should try next. We expect you to tell us when something is not working — especially when something is not working.
   

  

**What Success Looks Like — And How We Grow**
 This is not about vanity metrics. Ten people who genuinely use and value KindVoice can teach us more than thousands of passive followers. People who come to KindVoice may be lonely, having a difficult evening or simply wanting another person to hear them, so how we grow matters as much as how quickly we grow.
   

  

 We do not want aggressive growth hacking, spam, manufactured engagement or exaggerated promises. We will never exploit loneliness to acquire users. We want to find people for whom KindVoice genuinely makes sense, listen to what they tell us and build something they want to be part of.
   

  

 We care about genuine Listener interest and applications, active Listeners, Seekers who try the platform and return, completed conversations, honest feedback and communities that consistently bring the right people to KindVoice.
   

  

 Discover
   

  

 Learn the platform, map potential communities and start listening. Find out what people understand immediately, what needs explaining and what makes them hesitate.
   

  

 Experiment
   

  

 Test different communities, messages and approaches. Develop the channels showing promise and stop spending time on those that are not working.
   

  

 Validate
   

  

 Concentrate on the strongest approaches. Document what succeeded, what failed and what you believe KindVoice should do next.
   

  

 By the end, we want a clearer understanding of who our people are, where to find them and what makes them participate and stay.
   

  

 Who might be right for this
   

  

 There is no single career path we expect. You may have experience in community building, volunteer coordination, social\-impact work, university communities, communications or early\-stage startups. Your background may also be completely different.
   

  

 What matters more is how you think and how you work with people. You should be able to:
   

  

* Start thoughtful online conversations without sounding like a salesperson.
* Work independently and turn broad goals into practical experiments.
* Build relationships rather than rely on advertising or spam.
* Listen carefully to criticism, confusion and hesitation.
* Recognize when an approach is not working and propose a better one.
* Communicate clearly in spoken and written English.


 Additional languages are welcome. Experience with volunteer communities, peer support, NGOs or community\-led products would be particularly relevant.
   

  

 Working arrangement and how to apply
   

  

 This is a remote, part\-time freelance engagement for approximately
 **8–12 hours per week** 
 . You can work worldwide and will organize your own time using your own equipment.
   

  

 The initial engagement is for
 **three months** 
 . There will normally be one short meeting each week; other communication can largely be asynchronous. KindVoice.me email will be provided. If it works well for both sides, the collaboration can continue. Either side can end it with two weeks notice.
   

  

 Compensation is
 **USD 750–1,000 per month** 
 , depending on experience and level of involvement, paid weekly against invoice. This is an independent freelance/contractor engagement rather than employment.
   

  

 We do not need a perfect résumé. We are interested in how you think, what you notice and how you work with communities.
   

  

 The application asks you to upload your CV and answer these three questions directly:
   

  

* Why does KindVoice and this particular role interest you?
* Imagine you started working with us tomorrow. Where would you look for the first 100 potential KindVoice Listeners, and how would you approach them?
* Tell us about a community you have helped build, grow or engage. What did you personally do, and what did you learn?


 Please write the answers yourself. We are not interested in AI\-generated answers or cover letters.
   

  

 KindVoice is not trying simply to acquire users. We are trying to build a community people genuinely want to be part of.

title: Cluster Manager / Area Manager - North
description:
**Read this bit first:**




 We're not looking for someone to sit in an office, open a sales dashboard at 10 AM and ask, “Why are we down this week?” We're looking for the person who goes to the store, figures out why, fixes it, and makes sure it doesn't happen again.
 



  





 Uni Seoul is scaling fast — new cities, new stores, new teams, new challenges. And our Cluster/Area Managers are right in the middle of it.
 



  





 You'll own a cluster of stores like they're your mini businesses — sales, people, operations, inventory, customer experience and everything in between.
 



  





**The business we're building:**




 At Uni Seoul, we transform everyday life with Korean\-inspired design, cuteness, and functionality. From plush toys to stationery, and fashion accessories, our brand brings vibrant, Seoul\-inspired experiences to a young, trend\-focused audience. We're building a new kind of everyday retail — and we're scaling it across India.
 



  





 That means the operating playbook is still being written. You won't just be following the system. You'll help build it.
 



  





**The job, honestly:**



* Your stores are your business.
* You'll be responsible for what happens before opening, during peak hours, after closing and everything in between.
* Some days you'll be looking at regional numbers.
* Some days you'll be on the floor fixing execution.
* Some days you'll be hiring an SM.
* Some days you'll be dealing with a stock issue that absolutely cannot wait until tomorrow.
* And some days you'll be asking: “Why are we doing this this way?”



  





 That's the job.
 



  





**What you'll own:**




**The Business** 



* Own sales, productivity and commercial performance across the North cluster.
* Break down store performance — footfall, conversion, ATV, UPT, margins and productivity — and turn numbers into action.
* Identify what's holding a store back and build a plan to move it.
* Push stores beyond simply hitting targets — build businesses that are healthy and scalable.



**The Operations** 



* Own day\-to\-day operational excellence across stores.
* Keep inventory, replenishment, shrinkage, audits, VM, hygiene and SOP execution tight.
* Spot operational gaps before they become business problems.
* Build simple, scalable processes that actually work on the shop floor.
* Handle escalations, crises and those “this needs to be fixed right now” moments.



**The People** 



* Build, coach and challenge Store Managers to become stronger business owners.
* Create teams that know their numbers, understand their customers and take ownership.
* Identify future leaders and build the next layer of talent.
* Deal with performance issues early — not after they become resignation letters.
* Build a culture where high standards and high energy can coexist.



**The Customer** 



* Every Uni Seoul store should feel unmistakably Uni Seoul.
* You'll own the consistency — from how the store looks, to how the team sells, to how the customer walks out feeling.
* A good store sells products. A great store makes people want to come back.



**The Expansion** 



* We're opening new stores and entering new markets.
* You'll be involved in making those stores work — from team readiness and operational setup to launch execution and getting the business on track.



  





**You'll probably enjoy this if...**



* You've spent 8\+ years in retail operations and still like being on the shop floor.
* You naturally think in numbers \+ people \+ execution, not just one of the three.
* You can look at a P\&L and then walk into a store and figure out what's happening behind it.
* You're comfortable challenging Store Managers — and coaching them at the same time.
* You don't need everything to be perfectly structured before you start moving.
* You can make decisions with imperfect information and take accountability for them.
* You notice the little things — messy fixtures, poor replenishment, weak selling behaviour, unhappy teams — before they become big things.
* You like building things, not just maintaining them.



  





**Why Uni Seoul?**



* Your cluster isn't just a set of stores on a dashboard. It's a business you're expected to grow.
* We're scaling quickly, which means you'll actually see your decisions turn into reality.
* You won't need five meetings to get an idea moving.
* Our stores, teams and processes are growing with us — and you'll have a real say in how they evolve.
* We're building a national retail network. The opportunity grows as the business grows.



  





**One last thing..**




 We're not hiring someone to manage stores.
 



 We're hiring someone who can build better stores, better teams and a better business.
 



  





**If that sounds like your kind of retail, let's talk.** 




  





**Apply: talent@uniseoul.in**
